sourceEvidence.excerpt:
##### **Whole numbers: Apply place value to partition, regroup and rename numbers to 1 billion**

- Recognise 1000 thousands is 1 million and 1000 millions is 1 billion

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|The 'place value houses' showing 1000 million is 1 billion.|
||
|![A house representing separate place values for the number 1 000 000|
|000. Detail in text|
|below.](media/image2.png){width="4.259431321084865in"|
|height="0.9841666666666666in"}|
||
|*Image long description*: The 'place value houses' show the number 1|
|billion divided into each of its place values. Each group of three|
|digits is broken up into the billions, millions and thousands|
|columns, each of which then contains a hundreds, tens and ones|
|column.|
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Regroup numbers in different forms (Reasons about quantity)

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|Such as 163 480 spoken as 163 thousands, 4 hundreds and 8 tens|
|or one hundred and sixty-three thousand four hundred and eighty,|
|and written as $$100\ 000 + 60\ 000 + 3000 + 400 + 80$$.|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Partition numbers to 1 billion in non-standard forms

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|When adding 163 480 and 150 000, 163 480 could be partitioned as|
|$$150\ 000 + 13\ 480$$, so that 150 000 could then be doubled|
|and added to 13 480.|
||
|Such as 73 400 is 734 hundred.|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

theory.intro: When adding or subtracting numbers with different numbers of digits, line them up by place value so each column holds ones, tens, hundreds and so on.
facts: **Align the place values** (ones under ones, tens under tens) — line up the right-hand ends for whole numbers.
Add a column at a time, **regrouping** into the next column when the total reaches $10$ or more.
When adding three or more numbers, a column total can be larger than $19$ — carry the full tens part, including any amount carried from the previous column.

When subtracting, regroup if the top digit is smaller than the digit being subtracted. Exchange $1$ unit of the next place for $10$ units of the current place. If the next place contains $0$, regroup from a higher place first.
For a subtraction with three or more numbers, subtract the second number from the first, then subtract each remaining number from the running result in order.
steps: For addition, write all the numbers in a column, aligned by place value. For subtraction, align the running result and the next number to subtract.

Work from ones to tens to hundreds and continue through the remaining places. For addition, include any carried amount and regroup each column total as needed. For subtraction, regroup before subtracting whenever needed.
For subtraction, repeat with each remaining number in order.

methods.description: Add three or more whole numbers with different numbers of digits by aligning equal place values, working from ones towards higher places, including carried amounts and regrouping the full column total. The written column procedure implements the syllabus requirement; a filled column lesson is not supplied.

Subtract two or more whole numbers from a starting whole number in the stated order. Align each subtraction by place value, regroup where needed, and use the result for the next subtraction. Keep tasks within whole-number results; do not introduce negative-number arithmetic.

value.question_text: Calculate $42000+5123+246$ by grouping digits with the same place value.
Calculate $735+64+8$ by aligning the place values.
Calculate $3806+475+29$ by grouping digits with the same place value.
Calculate $8200+906+75+4$ by aligning the place values.

Calculate $5687+2498+936+79$.
Take care when a column total is greater than $19$.

A student rewrites $42000+5123+246$ as $42000+51230+24600$.
Explain the place-value error and calculate the original sum.
value.solution_text:
The student shifted the shorter numbers left instead of aligning their ones digits.
$42000+5123+246$
$=47369$

value.question_text:
Three numbers have a total of $25000$.
Two of the numbers are $18450$ and $675$.
Find the third number.

Calculate $6875+5489+3968$.
Show how you handle a column total greater than $19$.
value.solution_text:
In the ones column, $5+9+8=22$, so write $2$ ones and carry $2$ tens.
$6875+5489+3968$
$=12364+3968$
$=16332$

value.question_text:
Niko places $58$ in the hundreds and tens columns when adding $7240+583+58$, so it acts as $580$.
Explain the error and find the correct total.
value.solution_text:
$58$ has $5$ tens and $8$ ones, so its ones digit must align with the other ones digits.
$7240+583+58$
$=7823+58$
$=7881$
